subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw add LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should that behavior live in shared core activation, in channel plugins, or behind a new plugin API seam?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but it cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, logging retention, config contract, or long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting implementation.

options.title: Narrow to attention-window behavior
options.body: Defer LLM peeking and instead pursue a simpler mention-triggered timer window through the narrower related issue if that meets the product need.

options.title: Move behind plugin/API design
options.body: Defer core activation until a trusted observation or decision hook can safely support this as plugin-owned behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest history across the current group activation and inbound mention-policy surfaces that this decision would extend.
